answer: One concrete defense: anchor each agent identity to a non-transferable bond of a scarce asset, then slash it for misbehavior. An attacker flooding the network with an ocean of 1,000 sybils must post 1,000 separate bonds (say 50 tokens each) = 50,000 tokens locked and burnable. In the attestation graph every agent is a vertex; a dishonest vertex earns nothing yet keeps its bond at risk, so one slashing event destroys real capital that cheap spoofing never spent. Breaking it means buying 50,000 scarce tokens, pushing the price up and making the next sybil dearer.
